assumptions: A legitimate PARTIAL result may create some phase deliverables while others remain absent; partial acceptance is not full phase acceptance.
The supplied process, locking, authorization and protection interfaces are assumed to hold. Their implementations were not included in this review scope.
Workers are trusted and remain in the initial process group, as specified.
checks: Traced planning, plan rejection, editable repair, verification, result review and bounded continuation paths.
Checked pending-review creation and resumption against incomplete deliverables and evidence preservation.
Inspected acceptance guards: positive integer test counts, explicit registered-checker criteria and independent AGREE remain necessary.
Treated the reported 197 passing tests and supplied test names as supporting evidence only; no commands were run or test bodies inspected.
issues: P2 — Bounded partial review incorrectly requires every final deliverable to exist. In execute_phase, a non-scoped PARTIAL result with a positive test count enters bounded_partial_work review even when checks report missing deliverables. However, save_pending_review unconditionally adds every phase deliverable and phase['test_file'] to names, then calls evidence_hashes, which raises on any missing file. Consequently, legitimate incomplete work never reaches its bounded result reviewer or durable pending-review checkpoint; the outer exception handler instead sends it through another editable repair cycle with only the missing-evidence error. save_continuation already recognizes missing files, so these two persistence paths impose inconsistent requirements. Repair save_pending_review to distinguish bounded-partial checkpoints from full-acceptance checkpoints: require the actual work/check/approved-plan records, hash existing declared evidence, and explicitly record absent final deliverables. Validate that recorded presence/absence on resume, invalidating and rechecking when it changes. Keep the complete-file requirement for full acceptance.
next_actions: Add a regression in tests/test_accounting_master.py where a non-scoped phase returns PARTIAL, checks execute a positive number of tests, and a final deliverable remains missing. Verify that bounded review executes without an additional editable attempt caused solely by the missing deliverable.
Cover review unavailability and subsequent read-only resume for that incomplete checkpoint, plus invalidation when a previously absent deliverable appears.
Rerun the relevant controller checks and obtain a fresh review of the repair.
residuals: The exact catalog contracts and test bodies were not supplied; whether a current phase already encounters this defect is not established.

The packet does not define the required input-hash coverage for every checker. verification_input_errors accepts an absent or empty mapping, so freshness depends on checker contracts identifying all material inputs.
Process containment, exclusive ownership and reusable narrow command approval were assessed only through the stated interfaces, not independently verified.
The accepted 192-report source panel and scoped internal phase acceptance do not close accounting, scientific or human-acceptance gaps.

summary: Bounded partial review can be prevented by missing final deliverables, causing unnecessary editable repair instead of resumable read-only review.
